_comment: Neck corridor — mechanical neck pain / posture / post-whiplash gentle rehab; authored in-house (original instruction text; exercise mechanics are facts, phrasing is ours). Dan + his PT review, correct, and expand.

exercises.name: Seated Chin Tuck
instructions: Sit tall in a chair with your shoulders relaxed and your gaze level.
Glide your head straight back, drawing your chin in to make a gentle double chin — the nose keeps pointing forward, not down.
Feel a light lengthening at the base of the skull; the movement is small, and it should never be forced or painful.
Hold the tucked position while breathing normally, then release slowly back to neutral.

exercises.name: Supine Chin Tuck
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and, if it is more comfortable, a small folded towel under your head.
Nod your chin gently toward your throat, as if giving a slow, tiny 'yes', flattening the back of your neck toward the floor.
Keep the big muscles at the front of the neck soft — the work comes from small, deep muscles, so the effort should feel subtle.
Hold the nod without holding your breath, then let the head rest completely.

exercises.name: Chin Tuck with Head Lift
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and no pillow under your head.
Do your gentle chin nod first, and keep it for the whole exercise — the chin never juts toward the ceiling.
Keeping the nod, lift your head just a finger-width off the floor, as if sliding it out from under a sheet of paper.
Hold steady while breathing normally, then lower with control; end the set the moment the chin starts to poke upward or you feel any dizziness.

exercises.name: Isometric Neck Side Press
instructions: Sit tall with your chin gently tucked and your head in a comfortable neutral position.
Place your palm flat against the side of your head, just above the ear.
Press your head sideways into the palm as if tipping your ear toward that shoulder — but let nothing actually move; the hand matches the push exactly.
Build the pressure gradually to a firm but comfortable effort, hold while breathing steadily, then ease off just as gradually before switching sides.

exercises.name: Isometric Neck Flexion-Extension Press
instructions: Sit tall with your chin gently tucked and your gaze level.
Place your palm on your forehead and press your head forward into it without letting the head move.
Then lace your fingers behind your head and press straight back into them, again without movement.
Build each press slowly and release just as slowly — sudden starts and stops are what irritate a healing neck.

exercises.name: Upper-Trapezius Stretch
instructions: Sit tall and grasp the edge of the chair seat with the hand on the side you want to stretch — this anchors that shoulder down.
Let your head tip away from the anchored side, the ear sinking toward the opposite shoulder.
Rest your free hand lightly on the side of your head for a touch of extra weight, but never pull.
Settle into a mild pulling feeling along the side of the neck, hold and breathe, then lift the head back upright before switching sides.

exercises.name: Levator-Scapulae Stretch
instructions: Sit tall and anchor the side you want to stretch by grasping the chair seat with that hand.
Turn your head about halfway away from the anchored side, then look down as if checking the opposite armpit.
Rest your free hand lightly on the back of your head, letting its weight guide the stretch — guide, never yank.
Hold where you feel a comfortable pull from the top corner of the shoulder blade up into the back of the neck, then release slowly and switch sides.

exercises.name: Seated Scapular Retraction
instructions: Sit tall toward the front half of the chair with your arms relaxed at your sides.
Draw your shoulder blades back and down, as if tucking them into your back pockets.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears and the chin gently tucked — the squeeze lives between the shoulder blades, not up in the neck.
Hold the squeeze briefly, then let the blades glide fully apart before the next repetition.

exercises.name: Thoracic Extension over Chair
instructions: Sit in a chair whose backrest ends around the middle of your back, feet flat on the floor.
Support your head by lacing your fingers behind it, elbows pointing forward.
Lean back over the top edge of the backrest, arching your upper back while the lower back stays quiet.
Return to sitting tall between repetitions; if you feel pinching, arch a little less far, and if you feel light-headed, stop and rest.

exercises.name: Wall Angel
instructions: Stand with your heels a few inches from a wall and lean back so your buttocks, upper back, and the back of your head all rest against it, chin gently tucked.
Raise your arms into a goalpost shape, working to keep the elbows and the backs of the wrists against the wall.
Slide the arms slowly up the wall as far as they will go without anything peeling away, then slide back down to the goalpost.
Losing contact is the signal you have reached today's range — work just inside it rather than forcing through.

exercises.name: Seated Band Row
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs out in front, knees soft, and loop the middle of a resistance band around the arches of both feet, checking that it sits securely and cannot slip off.
Hold one end in each hand, sit tall, and tuck your chin gently so your head stacks over your shoulders.
Pull the band toward the sides of your lower ribs, letting the shoulder blades lead by drawing back and down.
Pause, then let the band draw your arms slowly forward — the return should take longer than the pull, and any sharp pain is the signal to stop for the day.

progressions.note: Progress once you can repeat a ten-second seated tuck with the surface muscles at the front of the neck staying soft.
Progress when ten-second supine nods stay steady and symptom-free with no chin jut on any repetition.
Add posture work once a five-second press at firm effort builds and releases smoothly on both sides.
Move on when both directions tolerate a slow five-second build and release without symptoms spreading toward the shoulder or arm.
Progress when every squeeze holds through a full breath with the shoulders staying down away from the ears.
Add band resistance once unloaded squeezes feel effortless through a full set and sitting posture no longer sags between repetitions.
Progress once you can arch over the backrest through a comfortable range with no pinching at the end of the motion.
Add the angled version once the straight side-bend gives only a mild pull that fades within a minute of releasing.
